title: Give the active link a clear style
summary: NavLink knows whether its destination is the active route.
introduction: NavLink knows whether its destination is the active route. Your task: Add a visible underline rule for .current.
learningObjectives: Add a visible underline rule for .current.
Explain the example for give the active link a clear style

blocks.text: NavLink knows whether its destination is the active route. You can use that state to show which page is selected.

Use React Router 7 framework mode, the continuation of Remix's framework approach. Save files at the shown app paths. Set ssr:false in react-router.config.ts for this browser-only course. React tooling is required.

blocks.code:
import {NavLink} from "react-router";
export default function Menu(){return <nav aria-label="Main"><NavLink to="/books" className={({isActive})=>isActive?"current":""}>Books</NavLink></nav>;}
blocks.title: Give the active link a clear style

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `aria-label` supplies a name to assistive technology. It should explain the same purpose as the visible control or graphic.

blocks.text: On the books route, the link receives the current class and active-page semantics.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Use more than colour when useful, such as an underline. Ensure the current class has a real CSS rule.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Add a visible underline rule for .current.
